sources.name: GOV.UK viability guidance
sources.fact: Guidance updated December 2025 sets principles for plan and decision viability, including infrastructure contribution expectations

sources.name: Draft London Plan 2026
sources.fact: Draft Plan published 16 July 2026 and remains consultation/draft policy rather than adopted development plan

sources.name: Draft London Plan making best use of land
sources.fact: Draft strategy links housing/employment growth to infrastructure sufficiency and identifies utilities/social infrastructure dependencies

sources.name: Draft London Plan homes chapter
sources.fact: Draft housing policies are prospective consultation context and do not override adopted plan until adoption

sources.name: Support for Housebuilding London Plan Guidance
sources.fact: March 2026 adopted guidance implements time-limited measures supporting housing delivery; eligibility remains scheme-specific

sources.name: London Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36
sources.fact: Programme offers up to £11.7bn funding across 2026-36 subject to programme rules and applications

sources.name: London Social and Affordable Homes funding guidance
sources.fact: Funding eligibility and additionality requirements are project-specific and do not imply award

sources.name: City Hall Developer Investment Fund
sources.fact: March 2026 fund aims to unlock/accelerate housing but finance is application and criteria dependent

sources.name: Housing delivery and capacity support
sources.fact: NHA LDN and ATLAS LDN provide support services; support availability is not planning consent or finance

sources.name: London Growth Plan
sources.fact: Growth Plan links housing, infrastructure, skills and transport to productivity and delivery

sources.name: London Infrastructure Framework
sources.fact: 2026 framework identifies strategic infrastructure pipeline/priorities but not parcel-specific delivery dates

sources.name: LBBD Local Plan 2037
sources.fact: Adopted September 2024 Local Plan remains the borough planning starting point while newer London Plan material is draft

examples: A plan housing target is not a parcel-specific deliverable unit count
Draft London Plan policy must not override the adopted development plan before adoption
Grant or investment fund existence does not prove a project has an award or finance
Support programme participation does not prove planning permission or viability
National viability guidance requires scheme-specific inputs and does not provide a universal margin
Infrastructure priority does not prove delivery timing for a candidate site
Time-limited planning/support routes require eligibility evidence and cannot be assumed
No future-growth promotion is assigned without parcel geometry plus project-specific planning, infrastructure and delivery evidence
